findings.current: Did you know Chairman Xiao was once branded a reactionary and sentenced to five years of hard labor in a pig slaughterhouse?
findings.defect: The English adds that he was formally sentenced. The Korean says he had a history of performing five years of labor there, without establishing a legal sentence.
findings.rationale: 전력을 한 is a statement of past history, while the source does not specify sentencing or another legal mechanism.
findings.replacement: Did you know Chairman Xiao was once branded a reactionary and spent five years doing hard labor in a pig slaughterhouse?

findings.current: Chairman Shao had a personal grudge against the Crown Prince Party, and after enduring years of hardship, he had risen to the highest position in the country.
findings.defect: The chairman's name is rendered as “Shao” here but as “Xiao” throughout the surrounding passage, creating an internal continuity error for the same person.
findings.rationale: 샤오 주석 refers to the same Chairman Xiao used in the surrounding English lines.
findings.replacement: Chairman Xiao had a personal grudge against the Crown Prince Party, and after enduring years of hardship, he had risen to the highest position in the country.

findings.current: So this was how father and son met their end.
findings.defect: “Met their end” commonly implies that both father and son died, but the source describes their downfall; the father is being sent away to spend the rest of his life in confinement and is not stated to have died.
findings.rationale: 끝장나는구나 conveys being ruined or finished in their circumstances, not necessarily dying.
findings.replacement: So this was how father and son ended up.

summary: Mostly faithful, with three minor defects involving an added legal mechanism, inconsistent name rendering, and an implication that may suggest the father has died.
